caption:
Joining Tarleton State is a 4-star prospect from Arizona, Wisconsin and Mississippi State, quarterback Braedyn Locke! ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

Locke spent last season at Arizona, two seasons at Wisconsin (2023-24) and one season at Mississippi State (2022).
 
At Wisconsin, he played in a combined 16 games, starting 12 games at quarterback, including the final nine in 2024. Across his tenure, he completed 240-of-448 passes for 18 touchdowns and 2,713 yards, averaging 169.6 passing yards per game. In 2024, he totaled 1,936 pass yards and 13 pass touchdowns, his best game coming against Purdue, where he threw for 359 yards and three touchdowns.

caption:
I’ve been playing this game since I was six years old. From the very beginning I had one dream—to play big-time football. What started on Pop Warner fields turned into a journey full of moves, setbacks, doubt, and risks that shaped who I am today.

Growing up, football was how I made friends and found my place. Especially after moving to a new state. When I got to high school, I was doubted from day one. My own head coach told me to my face that I would never play a down of college football. Instead of letting that define me, I took a leap of faith, moved again, and chased opportunity.

I earned varsity as a sophomore, trained on my own through COVID when we couldn’t practice and did everything I could to stay ready. Along the way, I trusted people I shouldn’t have—people who talked me up to my face but tore me down behind my back. Despite being All-Region my junior and senior years, doors I was promised never opened.

So I stopped waiting and created my own path. Chowan University in North Carolina gave me my first real opportunity, and I made the most of it. When the staff left, I bet on myself again and kept climbing—this time to Jackson State University, where I grew as a player and a man and earned some of the best accolades of my career Including All Conference and All American.

With all of this, I still wasn’t done. I took one last risk, entered the portal, and finally fulfilled my dream of playing big-time football at the University of Arizona. Looking back, every setback had a purpose.

Thank you football—for the lessons, the brotherhood, and the resilience. Without this game, I wouldn’t be the man I am today. But most importantly thank you to my family who has had my back this whole journey, this journey is nothing without them. But threw it all I’m glad to say I did things MY WAY❤️

¡NUEVA LEONA EN LA SELVA!

Las Leonas de Ponce reciben con orgullo a una nueva integrante que llega a sumar talento, compromiso y carácter competitivo.

Fue clasificada como la No. 2 recluta en su clase de secundaria y destacó como una de las mejores jugadoras juveniles de voleibol en EE. UU. durante su etapa escolar, incluyendo selecciones All-America y premios como Arizona Gatorade Volleyball Player of the Year. 

- USC Athletics
Comenzó su carrera universitaria en USC (University of Southern California) antes de transferirse para jugar en Arizona Wildcats para estar más cerca de su familia en Arizona. 

En Arizona se consolidó como una de las principales atacantes del equipo, liderando al conjunto en numerosas estadísticas ofensivas.
Arizona Desert Swarm 

• Logros y reconocimientos: 

Fue seleccionada All-Big 12 First Team (primera selección del torneo de conferencia) y obtuvo honores AVCA All-America honorable mention, una distinción destacada en voleibol universitario.

Ayudó a su equipo a ganar el NIVC Championship (NCAA Invitational Volleyball Championship) y a regresar al Torneo Nacional de la NCAA. 

Terminó su carrera universitaria superando los 1,500 puntos por puntos ofensivos, con más de 1,100 kills como jugadora de Arizona y un rendimiento destacado en kills por set a nivel nacional.

• Carrera profesional:

En noviembre de 2025 fue seleccionada en el draft de Major League Volleyball (MLV) por el equipo Grand Rapids Rise, siendo elegida como la 18ª selección general, lo que marca el inicio de su carrera profesional en voleibol.

caption: A lot has happened this year. I was out injured until the late March setting me back a lot and bringing me to a low. I was still able to quickly get back in shape and run better than I ever have. I set the second fastest 800m time in Arizona history, won a national title in St. Louis and got the chance to compete at the NCAA level in cross country. From here on out, I will use this year as a prime example to not let setbacks stop me from doing what I love. I will continue to try and be in top shape and treat my body as a temple. Aside from running, I met lots of people and got to travel to lots of places, my favorite being Japan. I hope I can carry this good energy into 2026 and continue to perform well as long as I don’t overwork myself and prevent injury from happening again. Thank you God for another year. I pray to be closer to you in 2026 🙏.

caption:
Wrapping up 2025 means wrapping up my time as a TTL Devo Team athlete… it feels a little bittersweet🥲🫶🏼
What started out as an application submitted on a whim turned into one of the most formative parts of my year.
From Oceanside back in April, taking my first steps onto the long course scene already feeling this massive sense of community behind me, to sharing the podium with Paula in Augusta, to feeling nothing but encouragement and support after Marbella from TTL fans near and far during what could have easily been one of the lowest moments of my year… 
I know it sounds dramatic, but this opportunity has truly meant the world to me. A million thank you’s to Eric and Paula for taking a chance on me and seeing me as an athlete worth investing in, and for becoming wonderful friends to me along the way🤍 and of course thank you to Be and Nick for being the biggest hype people and friends too😌
While I’ll be moving on from being a Devo Team athlete in 2026, you can still catch me repping my TTL gear for years to come✨ 
Stay tuned for some big announcements of what’s to come in the new year!!

#thattriathlonlife

She will teach:

caption:
Arizona 6’6 Wing Anthony Dell’Orso has been one of the most underrated players in the country this season.

Through his first four games he’s averaging 14/2/3 on 49/45/100 splits and has played a crucial role in Arizona’s 4-0 start to their season. 

Dell’Orso is one of the best shooters in the country who’s shooting 45% from three on high usage and is great at getting to his spots off ball with his movement shooting and has the ability to shoot off the dribble. He’s also a talented finisher who’s shooting 75% at the rim and is one of the best wing passers in CBB. Dell’Orso’s ability to play as a creator and off ball player at an high level for his size is extremely valuable.

A year without my dad and a week without our Stella girl… While this year has been tough in lots of ways, there’s something beautiful about carrying the spirit of someone you love so much with you through a world they’re no longer in.
I see my dad in my morning coffee, in the way I love my pets, in the way I laugh at my own jokes, and so many more simple everyday moments.
This year has been a big one for me, and on one hand, to feel like he’s missing that is devastating, but on the other, it feels like we’re doing this together in a way I never could have understood before.
May every hard day continue to remind me how lucky I am to have experienced this sort of love- how lucky I am to call this family my own🤍🪽

70.3 Worlds in the words of Taylor Swift: long story short it was a bad time, long story short I survived🥲✨
Went in to this one feeling so confident in myself and my prep, came away feeling quite defeated… but on the bright side, I know exactly what I need to do to become the athlete I know I can be🥹
I feel really sad to have let down everyone who has made feel so immensely supported this year, but so thankful to have all these wonderful people in my corner❤️‍🩹
Overall I’ve accomplished more than I imagined possible in this first season racing middle distance, and even though I didn’t get my fairytale ending, I’m pretty damn proud of myself🥹
If you need me, I’ll be back in Tucson, turning my weaknesses into strengths💪🏼 (after a much needed off season of course) Catch ya on the course jn 2026!!

World Championships Tokyo 2025

My first world championships was a magical experience. Getting to explore the city of Tokyo and end on some good attempts at a PR bar, there’s not much more I could ask for! I ended in 22nd with 188.

Excited to watch the finals and get some well needed rest after the longest competition season of my life, I promise I’m done for this year now😅🇺🇸🤍

caption:
Polynesian college football player Shancco “Ise” Matautia is celebrating the pride, power, and presence of Polynesian athletes in college sports through his newly launched apparel brand — Island State University.

The idea was born during his summer internship with the McGuire Center for Entrepreneurship at the University of Arizona’s Eller School of Management, where Ise transformed a personal vision into a business. What began as an exploration of identity and culture quickly evolved into a brand built around his most important value — family.

With Island State University, Ise’s mission is to honor his heritage, share the Polynesian story, and carry that sense of family beyond the locker room — into Tucson and far beyond.

caption:
I got baptized back in May and it was one of the most meaningful and transformative moments of my life!! As a follower of Jesus, I believe with all my heart that He died for our sins so that we could have eternal life with Him. Getting baptized was my way of taking the next step in my faith.

I’ve learned that my worth comes from God alone. No matter what season of life I am going through I trust that God is always guiding me to the perfect plan He has for me.

Since choosing to walk with Christ, I’ve experienced a peace and joy that can only come from God. I’m no longer anxious about what’s to come because I know He’s in control. I now look at failures and fear as opportunities to grow. I don’t need to have everything figured out, I just need to trust Him.

Each day I strive to live my life like Jesus lived His. I’m far from perfect, but I know He’s with me through it all.

“Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone, the new is here!” – 2 Corinthians 5:17

caption:
[TW Suicidal Thoughts/Attempts] 

Believe him or not but believe me when I say I tried to commit and failed many times and I had no motivation in me to keep on living. I tried to commit at least once a year since the age of 12, and countess crying nights and depression days. 

I hated God, adored and victimized satan, but I never understood when I chose to be on satans side, believe in atheist propaganda, hyper liberal propaganda, I was still depressed and suicidal. Therapy didn’t work at the time, I was desperate for love, acceptance, and a relationship, and people to like me. 

Near the end of my sophomore year of juco, all options to be less depressed and suicidal were attempted and failed. I researched other religions (besides Christianity) and none of them clicked. I wasn’t going to compromise my morals to attain my desires or hopes. I was so tired of it, but then suddenly a thought popped in my head. 

I didn’t try one thing, and that was actually taking a chance on Jesus, on Christianity entirely. I told myself if it didn’t work, I would attempt again and I will make sure to succeed with it. 4 years later I have been healed by God with my suicidal thoughts and tendencies. 

I have completely changed, repented, and I want to break the negative stigmas of Christianity. And my whole motivation to living in this broken cruel world is when everyone who has or will encounter me, they will see God, who loves, cares, and wants them to know him. So me, who hated him, spread his hate of God, was literally on the enemy’s side can be transformed by God and accepted by him, so can you. 

#christianity #christian #testimony #foryoupage #orthodoxy #jesuschrist #godisgood #christianwomen #sucideprevention #mentalhealth #mentalwellness

caption:
6 months of locked-in training. 20 pounds of muscle. A full transformation.

When @porter.patton first committed to the University of Arizona, the plan was to gray shirt—get some extra time to develop before officially joining the squad. Undersized for his position but not lacking heart, he made a decision: outwork the timeline.

Since day one at Helix, Porter showed up with purpose.
He trained with intent. He moved with discipline.
And the results followed.

Porter went from 260 to 280 lbs of explosive strength, improved his speed, and became one of the most athletic defensive linemen on the roster. Arizona took notice—and instead of waiting, they told him to report early.

The lesson for young athletes?
Development wins.
The weight room matters.
Consistency over hype.
You don’t need to chase validation—just chase growth.

The work will always speak.

#PorterToZona #HelixPerformance #AthleteDevelopment #EarnedNotGiven #SpeedStrengthPower #HighSchoolToCollege #TrainToDominate #FootballJourney #HelixBuilt

caption:
TOMORROW // #156 - Lydia Russell, Professional Triathlete 

In this deeply honest and moving episode, professional triathlete Lydia Russell shares the journey that brought her from a childhood of competitive swimming to the pro triathlon circuit—all while carrying the weight of personal loss and learning to lead with both her head and her heart.

Lydia opens up about her nonlinear path through college athletics, the coaching struggles that almost broke her, and the pivotal mindset shifts that helped her find joy and purpose in training again. She shares how losing her father just 7 months ago reshaped her perspective on life, racing, and what it means to leave an impact. From her spiritual roots in Quaker schooling to her candid thoughts on mental health, grief, and identity, Lydia invites us into her world with depth, vulnerability, and humor.

This is not just a conversation about racing—it’s about resilience, legacy, and learning to show up fully, even when life hits hard.

Been racing 🙂

Had the opportunity to compete in three incredible races over the past few weeks. Super happy with the results and learning takeaways! I started the trip in Colombia for the Americas Triathlon Championships Calima where I placed third to round out a USA podium! Then went to Austria for the Europe Triathlon Junior Cup Wels where I placed second. Then finally headed to the Netherlands for the Europe Triathlon Junior Cup Holten where I placed 6th. These races have been super encouraging by showing me a lot of my new strengths and also where I need some improvement. Excited to get back to training before the next one!!

caption:
European Cup Rzeszów 🇵🇱 and 11th place for me!

My first European Cup and first Olympic distance race of the season – and definitely lots of takeaways.

A tough swim put me into the chase group early on, and even though we tried to catch the front pack, they were getting further away each lap.

BUT I finished the race with a strong run, probably one of my best so far, which helped me climb up to just outside the top 10. For the first time in a couple years I was actually happiest and felt the most confident with that last part of the race.
This race showed improvement 🏃‍♀️ over the past months, and that means so much to me. Grateful for the experience and proud of the progress! 🙏💪 Even though with a better start, there was definitely potential for a stronger result.

Shoutout to my dad for traveling with me, taking photos, and giving me time splits during the race – first time ever my parents came this far for a race!😂

caption:
Spring🌺
Decided to highlight some of my favorite moments from this spring semester. It’s been full of funny memories with my team, lots of sunshine, way too many 6 am practices 😂, and hours of hard, consistent training that we hope will soon pay off. There were some tough days at school too, and plenty of exhaustion along the way — but also so many experiences that helped us grow and learn.

Some of the standout moments: winter training, kicking off the season with 9th place at the America’s Cup, pretending to be a dentist (still not qualified 😅), celebrating Arizona Athletics at CATSYS, and of course, Gabi’s, Grandma Lydia’s, and Laura’s graduations 🥺🎓👏, renting 🤔 Molly’s dragon 🐉 and many more.

I'm so grateful for this team — for pushing me, supporting me, and making this semester such a unique experience. We challenged each other, lifted each other up, and made memories I’ll never forget.

Next stop: race block in Europe 🤪🫶 If you’ve made it this far, leave a comment ⬇️😄

caption:
First collegiate season is done ✅ 

It was a hard one for me because in my eyes I wasn’t preforming how I wanted to, but I realize that it’s normal to have downs. Success doesn’t come from someone starting at that top and staying there for the entire season. Hard work pays off and I try my best to do just that. God had a plan for me this season and he has one for the next. It’s just up to me to trust that plan. 

I want to personally thank my teammates and coach(es) Being on this team with you guys has been the most special experience I’ve ever had. I built friendships and managed to have fun despite being homesick sometimes. Even for this meet, many of you came out, sent texts or videos showing your support for me. I appreciate all the love you’ve given me throughout this semester and I pray we can make more memories in the future.

Mom and Dad. You guys always talk about how amazing your children are, but I need to remind you that we are this way because of you guys. You guys are the greatest blessing in my life and you pushed me in ways that I never knew was possible, and that’s gotten me here. You both deserve credit too. Thank you for all the love you’ve given me for over 19 years. ❤️❤️

caption:
JV -> Varsity ->Juco-> D1 = 10 years invested into the sport. 

Testimony: I believe God made me have this path to show the example that anything is truly possible through hard work, dedication, sacrifice, prayer, and having faith! I have lived an answered prayer with Track and Field. 

And context too, I hated God throughout High school, was a hater atheist, so him still answering what you’re about to read, that’s his compassion, love and mercy he has on us. 

From JV I prayed for Varsity. From varsity I prayed to either go to MCC and train with @sprint_ambassador and @keiap23 or else I will stop track right then and there. It was answered. From Juco I prayed to God, now having a more developed relationship with him- i really deeply prayed with tears that @franchise2121 will give me a chance, I didn’t want to go anywhere else but @arizonatrack . My dream to compete at the highest level possible and what other Juco kids and high schoolers dream about. And it was answered by the Grace of God, it was a half court and made it in because of her and Him. I’ll forever be grateful to Coach Greene for that and I’ll praise him forever for that. 

it was an answered prayer that is a part of my joy, but the greatest joy I have within track and field is me finding God in this sport. And him leading me to the relationships that I will cherish and show his love to. 

The author for this track and field chapter of my life and it has ended. But he isn’t done with the book yet. I’m excited to see what’s in store.

He died for me so I will live for him. That’s why I Love this Story (get it hehe) Praise the Lord, Praise the Lord in all circumstances.

caption:
Don’t overcook a steak. 
The same principle applies to coaching. I often see coaches as chefs—too much seasoning or time on the flame, and the meal is ruined. Training works the same way: an excess of one element can lead to stagnation, regression, or even injury.

As coaches, our role is to balance intensity and volume with precision, adjusting them in harmony with performance goals and the competitive calendar.

And just like the journey from sous chef to head chef, or from a local kitchen to a Michelin-starred restaurant, our growth depends on exposure—stepping into new environments, learning from different coaching philosophies, and always refining our craft.

Stay sharp. Stay curious . Keep learning.

caption:
REGENTS CUP INFO:
It is a tri-university competition held and sponsored by the Arizona Board of Regents. It gives an opportunity for students from ASU, NAU, and UofA to debate through civil discourse and win scholarships if you make it through to the finals. The Regents decide what topics are being discussed each year and this year was mainly about state and federal power. 
This was my second year representing UofA at the Regents Cup and I have grown so much as a debater as someone who has never had that experience before. I definitely recommend this for those who want to improve public speaking skills and have an interest in a law career. We learn how to do specific research and work with a partner when expressing ideas and how to maintain an informed conversation about difficult topics with others.
It is very time consuming but also a lot of fun and progress is seen on a week to week basis. The season lasts from November to March usually. Follow @uadiscourseseries to be a part of it next year!
1st place scholarship: 15,000$
2nd place scholarship: 12,000$
3rd place scholarship: 5,000$
500$ for participation
#explore #speechanddebate #regentscup

caption:
An inside look at what our early acceleration days look like. We always start the week with acceleration work, since I consider it medium intensity with low muscular damage. It puts us in a sweet spot—not too light coming off the weekend, but not so intense that guys feel sluggish and underperform.

It also sets the tone for the rest of the week, leading into our top speed work mid-week and COD work to finish strong.

Primer/Testing:

• Split stance overcoming iso

• Med ball reverse granny toss for distance

• CMJ

Tech Work:

• Shin angle marches

• Resisted staggered stance broad jumps

• Resisted marches

Main Work:

• Fly sprints

• 40% velocity decrement on the T-Apex

caption: Yup…that just happened today. 11 months and 20 days ago I tore my ACL and MCL of my right leg. I did my whole rehab and was back playing after 9 months. I felt like nothing could stop me cause I just overpassed adversity and was super excited for season. Unfortunately, I tore my left MCL and ACL today. The rollercoaster of emotions I am experiencing is actually insane. Back to back ACLs?! It is actually crazy. Even though I am going through one of the lowest points of my life, the support system I have that includes my parents, my teammates, my coaching staff, my friends, and my God will help get through it all. It sounds crazy but I will do the whole process all over again and come back even more stronger and better. Even though I don’t see the silver lining now, I will focus on the process and on getting better one day at a time. So with all of this being said…PA ENCIMA PUÑETA 💗💗💗💗💗

caption:
Bye 2024! 

Life Motto: “I could die right now happy I served a friend That died for my life; our love goes hand-in-hand.”

This year taught me how to truly love God, all things him and all his creations (you 🫵). But the teachings often come with trials, and hardships. It’s not only to test our faith but our heart. Do truly want to know God and follow him (ME ME I DO I DO) 

This year definitely humbled me. I started off pursuing God for the perks/exceptions to achieve worldly glory (track accomplishments, relationships, etc) but He is not a genie lamp!! And all worldly things fade away, and last for only a little bit until death. But I know a guy who defeated death, so I’m always going to listen to him instead of the world. 🌎 

I am forever blessed because of Him, the protector, the redeemer, the provider, the savior, the kings of kings, and the Lord of Lords. I love you dearly, Jesus of Nazerath ✝️

Tomorrow is not ever promised. Thank God for today and future today’s. And take every day to greatest commandments: to Love God with all you have! And to Love People much more than yourself.

caption:
NCAA National Champions,🥉in the individual and a freshman of the year!

This season had a many 📈📉 and the fact that I will lose the opportunity to race at the European and World Championships in my final junior year was very hard to take… However, this did not stop us from believing and consistently preparing.

I would like to thank to the whole @arizonatriathlon for making every day unique and amazing! We did it! Thank you to my coaches @coachwes and @jossibonney and all the support team Jessie Johnson, @dayannara.munoz , @nic.zarat for believing in me and supporting me in every step of the way ❤️💙

I would also like to express how grateful I am for everyone believing and supporting me back home @trisport.triathlon.team , Kamzík 1000+, @cyklostore and @jana_smidakova 

Thank you @duklabanskabystrica , @slovenskyolympijskytim and @slovak_triathlon_union for your continuous support.

I am so grateful and honoured to be surrounded by such amazing people!

Finishing the season like this is much more than I thought I could’ve dream about! And looking back at my junior years I couldn’t have asked for more. It was a blast! Thank you Jozef Vrábel 🫶🏼

Now it’s time to get some rest 🏝️/📚😬 🤷‍♀️ 

Season 2025 here I come! 🤩😼

caption: In honor of breast cancer awareness month, I wanted to share about someone special to me. Someone who I keep close to me on and off the field. Dace, was a breast cancer fighter not just once but twice. I only knew Dace for a short amount of time, but she made a lasting impact on my life as if I was her own. Dace was a warrior, a fearless leader, a loving mother and a kindhearted friend. She was a light in every room, touching so many lives. Breast cancer won the battle. But she continues to shine her light in so many lives. She is my why. My good luck charm. She reminds me to play with joy, to enjoy every opportunity God has given me, to always be a fighter in life's battles and be a light in as many lives as possible. One of Dace's favorite things was a purple lily and I will continue to honor her and shine her light everyday💜💜💜

Primera carrera en Europa, con un buen resultado para lo contratiempos que hubieron. Tres semanas antes de la carrera, después de un trabajo en la pista me fracture el quinto metatarso del pie izquierdo. Ya había dado por perdida la carrera y me salí del start list. Pero a la semana y media decidí correr con lo que tuviera. 

No pude llevar a la final, pero sin dudas di lo mejor que pude a pesar de que no puede entrar como lo planeado y que mi pie no estaba totalmente recuperado.

Muchas gracias @marcos.lucero.925 por ayudarme a recuperar mi pie lo antes posible, y convencerme de competir, aunque sea por la experiencia. También gracias a la federación argentina por el apoyo en todas mis idas y vueltas con la inscripción. 

Thank you very much @coachwes @jossibonney for the support even though we are very far away. It's time to rest, get my foot back and continue this journey together 🫶🏼

caption: Experiencing this ACL tear was tough. The pain, the uncertainty-it was overwhelming. But I decided early on that I was not going to let this defeat me. There were moments when I wondered if Id ever make it back to the old me, if all the hard work would pay off. All of the rehabs, crying, wondering, and moments where I felt like giving up motivated me to keep pushing through. I kept pushing, day in and day out, determined to prove to myself that I could overcome this obstacle. Leaning on the right people and having the people I had around made this process ten times easier. Finally, I can now say that I am cleared and will be back on the court. This was such a humbling moment, and a reminder of just how far I have come. God put me in this position to come back stronger than before and more prepared. This is not the end of my journey, it it just the beginning of a new chapter.

Not an ideal nationals, but I still feel incredibly grateful to claim my 3rd and last SA junior title ❤️‍🔥
